method: Whole-file manual reading of6files; bytes compared with pinned Git objects. No Windows UI/ACL runtime execution.
findings: Permission page validates5account regexes and level selection ranges plus exclusion regex before staging settings; effect invalidates rule colors and notifies list repaint. Transaction commit belongs to previously reviewed shared settings framework.
Prompt page stages14checkbox bindings, builds localized operation-specific confirmation labels. Changing settings does not execute those operations.

Permission item owns shared snapshot CItem and ACL account/mask/deny/flags data; GetLinkedItem only resolves to current scan tree while settled, matching stored path and exact child names. Snapshot row is not immutable live filesystem identity.

ComputeRightsLevel selects first cumulative bitmask fully contained in one ACE mask; deny flag displayed separately. This is rights summarization, not AccessCheck/token evaluation or combination of ordered allow/deny ACL entries.
ComputeApplies maps OI/CI/IO flags for containers; file rows always apply to themselves. Additional propagation flags are not represented by that simplified classification.

Color rules compiled on version change, use case-insensitive account regex and first matching rights threshold; invalid regex from persisted values silently skipped. No bound on pattern complexity or runtime regex budget shown.
Localized rights/type/scope/yes-no labels are cached in function statics; switching language may retain initial cached names. Actual UI language-switch behavior untested.

Permission snapshot icon lookup is asynchronous and uses stored path/attributes; lifetime correctness still depends on control teardown and request guards examined earlier. Full permission scan control remains unread.
limits: No effective-access correctness, ACL corpus, UI transaction or platform runtime qualification.
No foreign production code adopted; native pHash investigation deferred.
